topic: Where do penguins live on the equator? (Galápagos penguin)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

iucn_galapagos_penguin.publisher: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
iucn_galapagos_penguin.title: Spheniscus mendiculus (Galápagos Penguin)
iucn_galapagos_penguin.notes: Endangered; population about 1,200 mature individuals; endemic to the Galápagos (Ecuador), mostly Fernandina and western Isabela; range map/assessment: breeding mainly Fernandina and Isabela, the latter straddling the equator

wiki_galapagos_penguin.title: Galápagos penguin
wiki_galapagos_penguin.notes: the only penguin found north of the equator; most on Fernandina and the west coast of Isabela; Humboldt and Cromwell Currents keep it alive at tropical latitude; northern tip of Isabela crosses the equator so some live in the Northern Hemisphere; ~1,200 mature as of 2018; 48–50 cm, 2–4 kg; IUCN Endangered

wiki_isabela.title: Isabela Island (Galápagos)
wiki_isabela.notes: largest Galápagos island; the equator crosses its northern part (Volcán Wolf / Ecuador volcano area)

gct_penguin.title: Galápagos penguin
gct_penguin.notes: only penguin species found north of the equator; one of the rarest penguins; population swings with El Niño

earth_org_penguin.title: Galapagos Penguin: Endangered Animals Spotlight
earth_org_penguin.notes: IUCN Endangered; population approximately 1,200; endemic to the Galápagos

penguinsg.title: Galapagos Penguin
penguinsg.notes: likely the rarest penguin; Endangered (IUCN 2020); breeds mostly on northern/eastern Fernandina and south-western Isabela

claims.text: The Galápagos penguin (Spheniscus mendiculus), endemic to the Galápagos Islands of Ecuador, is the only penguin species found north of the equator.
vo: where do penguins live on the equator
the only penguin north of the equator lives here

claims.text: The northern tip of Isabela Island crosses the equator, so some Galápagos penguins live in the Northern Hemisphere — the only penguins to do so. Most live on Fernandina and western Isabela.
vo: isabela's northern tip crosses the line, so some nest in the northern hemisphere

claims.text: The cool Humboldt and Cromwell Currents let the species survive at a tropical latitude.
vo: cold humboldt and cromwell currents keep the water cool

claims.text: IUCN lists the species as Endangered with about 1,200 mature individuals — one of the rarest penguins.
vo: about twelve hundred adults remain, one of the rarest penguins alive

myths.myth: Penguins only live in Antarctica / cold places.
myths.reality: Most species live on temperate coasts; the Galápagos penguin lives on the equator thanks to cold currents.
No penguin lives in the Arctic; the Galápagos penguin is the only one that reaches the Northern Hemisphere, by a few kilometres.
